# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — a 1:1 replacement of `x.hasOwnProperty(k)` with `Object.hasOwn(x, k)`; behavior-preserving; no new concept.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** I read all 39 replaced lines at `e1e358eab2` against their receivers.
- Every ordinary-object site is equivalent, including primitive receivers: `Object.hasOwn('str', k)` boxes the same way `'str'.hasOwnProperty(k)` did.
- Two sites change only on edges, both in the safer direction:
  - `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs` — `(value && Object.hasOwn(value, 'bubble'))` no longer throws on a nullish `value`. The old `?.` guarded the method, not the receiver. A null-prototype listener object now has its own `bubble` honored instead of skipped.
  - `src/state/Provider.mjs` — `stores && …` keeps the old falsy result in its `if`.
- No receiver is a Proxy whose `get` trap would have answered `hasOwnProperty` differently.
- No Neo class overrides `hasOwnProperty`.
- The webpack configs run on Node ≥ 16.9.
- CI is green (50 pass, 1 skip).

The one miss is scope: `Resolves #3130` closes "replace all occurrences", but `docs/app` still carries four instance-method calls of the same shape.

**Findings:**

- [ ] Include the four `docs/app` call sites, so the close target is true when it closes: `docs/app/view/classdetails/HierarchyTreeList.mjs:85` (`item?.hasOwnProperty('augments')` → `item && Object.hasOwn(item, 'augments')`, keeping its nullish guard), and `docs/app/view/classdetails/MembersList.mjs:248`, `:358`, `:362`. Leave as they are: the vendored `highlight.pack.js`, the comments that name the property (`src/Main.mjs:508`, `WorkerErrorMirror.spec.mjs:77`), and the tests' `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(…)` form, which is already the receiver-safe idiom. Converting the tests is optional.
